belongs_to: Section 8.1 Figure it out, book p.191, Q.2 'Take a central line of a different length and try to draw the wave on it.' - printed answer wave
description: A wave made of exactly 4 identical semicircles (half circles) whose diameters lie on one horizontal straight 'central line'. Left to right the semicircles go: UP (above the line), DOWN (below), UP, DOWN. Each semicircle has the same diameter, so the central line is 4 equal diameters long; each semicircle is a true half circle (height equal to its radius, about half its width). The central line is a thick horizontal line with a filled black dot at its left end (start of the first up-semicircle) and a filled black dot at its right end (end of the last down-semicircle). The semicircles join each other on the central line at the 3 inner meeting points (no dots there). A text label 'central line' is written above the right part of the figure with a short downward arrow from the label to the central line; the arrow touches the line above the middle of the 4th (down) semicircle, where no upper arc is drawn. Line weight of curves and central line is the same (thick).
unclear: Exact width-to-height proportions read from the picture only (each semicircle about 235 px wide and 120 px high in a 983 px page image).

belongs_to: Section 8.2 Figure it out, book p.194, Q.3 'Draw at least 3 rotated squares and rectangles on a dot grid. Draw them such that their corners are on the dots. Verify...' - printed answer drawing
description: A rectangular dot grid of plain small black dots with equal spacing, 8 columns by 9 rows (72 dots, counted: 9 rows of 8). Three tilted (rotated) shapes are drawn on it as thin black outlines (no fill, no letters, no measurements), every corner sitting exactly on a dot. Use grid positions (column 1-8 from the left, row 1-9 from the top). (a) Small tilted SQUARE at the upper left with corners (col2,row2), (col4,row3), (col3,row5), (col1,row4); every side goes 2 dots across and 1 dot down (or 1 across and 2 down), side length sqrt(5) grid units, area 5 square units. (b) Tilted RECTANGLE at the upper right with corners (col6,row1), (col4,row2), (col6,row6), (col8,row5); its short sides go 2 across and 1 down (sqrt(5) units), its long sides go 2 across and 4 down (2 x sqrt(5) units), so the long side is exactly twice the short side, area 10 square units; each long side passes through one extra dot at its middle ((col5,row4) on the left long side, (col7,row3) on the right long side). (c) Larger tilted SQUARE at the bottom with corners (col2,row6), (col5,row5), (col6,row8), (col3,row9); every side goes 3 across and 1 down (or 1 across and 3 down), side length sqrt(10) units, area 10 square units. The small square and the rectangle do not touch; the rectangle's left corner (col4,row2) is close to the square's right corner (col4,row3) but separate; the bottom square's top corner (col5,row5) is just below the small square's bottom corner (col3,row5) on the same row and well apart from the rectangle's bottom corner (col6,row6). The shapes do not overlap.
unclear: Grid corner positions were read from an upscaled page image; counts of 8 columns and 9 rows were checked by pixel position.
